source.repository: external: rust-lang/regex (https://github.com/rust-lang/regex), cloned locally for this review

groundTruth.description: A genuine non-security correctness fix (not security/DoS, unlike 010-013): Regex::replacen's old logic inferred 'no match occurred' from `last_match == 0`, but last_match is also 0 when a real match occurs at position 0 with zero length (e.g. the anchor `^` matching an empty string at the start of the text) - so replacen incorrectly returned the original text unchanged instead of performing the replacement. The fix uses a peekable iterator and checks `it.peek().is_none()` to correctly distinguish 'no match at all' from 'a zero-width match at position 0'. Second non-security correctness case after 008, and the second in Rust after 010/012.

evidence.note: replacen's corrected no-match detection via a peekable iterator

groundTruth.confirmingFix: this commit itself; see the linked issues #393/#394 and the added regression test in tests/replace.rs
